fun_fact.headline: The dot above an i or j is called a tittle
fun_fact.body: The small dot above a lowercase i or j has its own name, the tittle. It appeared in medieval Latin manuscripts around the 11th century to tell the two letters apart in crowded handwriting; its name comes from the Latin titulus, the same root as the word title.

puzzle.title: The Open Field
puzzle.body: A man is found dead in the middle of a large open field, wearing a backpack, with no people, roads, vehicles or footprints for miles. What happened?
puzzle.approach: Question how the man got there in the first place.
puzzle.answer: His parachute failed to open; the backpack is the parachute. He arrived from above, which is why there are no footprints or roads.

word_puzzle.title: Pour Decisions
word_puzzle.body: Centre letter A; outer C, D, E, N, R, T. Words of 4+ letters, all containing A, only these seven letters; find the pangram.
word_puzzle.approach: Every word must include the centre A; the pangram uses all seven letters.
word_puzzle.answer: Pangram DECANTER (also RECANTED, CANTERED). Others: DARE, CADRE, TRADE, CATER, CRATE, TRACE, REACT, DANCE, ENACT, DECANT, RECANT, CANTER, NECTAR, TRANCE, ARDENT, NEATER, RANTED, DARTED.

notes: India and UK News could not be sourced: all their allowed outlets (The Hindu, Indian Express, Hindustan Times, Times of India, NDTV, Economic Times; BBC, Sky News) were unreachable due to a persistent network egress block, confirmed across 3+ retry attempts via WebSearch, WebFetch and proxied fetches. Both show a placeholder card rather than an off-list source. Several Misc-allowed outlets (BBC, Reuters, AP, Guardian, New Scientist, Ars Technica, NYT) were also blocked; Misc ran on Scientific American, the only reachable frontier-science outlet with fresh in-window items. Business was thinned by the US Independence Day market holiday. 27 verified news items across six reachable sections (SG 5, Global 5, Tech 4, Business 4, Sports 5, Misc 4), above the 8-item floor.
